primitives.name: Stochastic Bandit Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: The first four chapters are on IID rewards, from the basic model to impossibility results to Bayesian priors to Lipschitz rewards.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'K': 'number of arms (dimensionless)', 'T': 'time steps (dimensionless)', 'r_{i,t}': 'reward from arm i at time t (units of reward)'}
primitives.assumptions: Rewards are independently and identically distributed per arm; unknown mean rewards define arm value.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When reward distributions change over time or depend on context, IID assumption fails.

layer2.mapping: GSI's Bayesian inference engine maps observed rewards to posterior beliefs about arm values, while GSE uses these to update Q-values for action selection.
layer2.telemetry: Cumulative regret vs. optimal policy performance

primitives.name: Adversarial Bandit Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: The next three chapters cover adversarial rewards, from the full-feedback version to adversarial bandits to extensions with linear rewards and combinatorially structured actions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'r_{i,t}': 'reward from arm i at time t (units of reward)', 'x_{i,t}': 'context vector at time t (dimensionless)', 'w_{i,t}': 'weight vector (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Rewards may be chosen by an adversary; no distributional assumptions on rewards.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When environment is hostile or unpredictable, stochastic models fail due to lack of stationarity.

layer2.mapping: GSE employs online convex optimization techniques derived from adversarial bandits to compute robust action policies under worst-case reward sequences.
layer2.telemetry: Regret bound against adversarial sequence of rewards

primitives.name: Contextual Bandit Extension
primitives.verbatim_quote: Chapter 8 is on contextual bandits, a middle ground between IID and adversarial bandits in which the change in reward distributions is completely explained by observable contexts.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'x_t': 'context vector at time t (dimensionless)', 'a_t': 'action taken at time t (dimensionless)', 'r_t': 'reward received at time t (units of reward)'}
primitives.assumptions: Reward depends on both action and context; contexts explain variation in reward distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When context is unobservable or insufficiently informative, contextual bandit models degrade to standard bandits.

layer2.mapping: GSI leverages contextual bandits to infer player skill profiles from match data, while GSE applies this to select optimal tactical moves based on game state.
layer2.telemetry: Improvement in prediction accuracy over baseline models using context

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of multi-armed bandits lies in balancing exploration and exploitation under uncertainty. In stochastic settings, arms yield IID rewards, allowing for Bayesian updating of beliefs. Adversarial models assume worst-case reward generation without distributional assumptions. Contextual variants extend these by incorporating side information that explains reward variability. These primitives form a hierarchy where each builds upon prior assumptions—starting with IID, moving to adversarial, and finally to contextual. Dualities emerge in how regret bounds translate across models: e.g., lower bounds in stochastic settings imply upper bounds in adversarial ones through duality principles. Failure modes include model misspecification (e.g., assuming IID when rewards are adversarial) or insufficient context representation leading to poor generalization. Each primitive enables distinct reasoning pathways: Bayesian inference for GSI’s predictive modeling, regret-minimizing strategies for GSE’s adaptive play, and contextual adaptation for both systems.
